sections.title: APB4 to TL-UL Bridge Design Specification

sentences.text: Purpose: Normative design contract for architecture, RTL, verification, DFT, and physical integration of this IP.
Requirement terms: shall = mandatory and testable; should = recommended; may = optional.
Every mandatory requirement has a stable REQ-- identifier and a verification method.
Decisions agreed with the designer on 2026-10-18 are recorded in section 20.
Important limitation, read first: the bridge accepts only full-strobe writes (PSTRB = 4'b1111) and word-aligned addresses (PADDR[1:0] = 2'b00).
A write with any other PSTRB value, and any access with a misaligned address, completes with PSLVERR = 1 and no TL-UL request is issued (DEC-001, REQ-ERR-001, REQ-ERR-002).
Software that needs byte or half-word writes must use a different bridge.

The bridge lets one APB4 Requester (for example a peripheral subsystem or a debug port) access a TL-UL fabric or device of the OpenTitan type.
It is an APB4 Completer on one side and a TL-UL host (manager) on the other.
Each APB transfer becomes one TL-UL request, and the TL-UL response becomes the APB completion.

The design goals are low latency and clean timing: the TL-UL request is launched from flip-flops in the first APB access cycle (see "early launch" in section 5.3), every output that changes toward either bus comes directly from a flip-flop, there is one clock domain, and the APB-facing logic and the TL-UL-facing logic are in separate modules.

Included: APB4 Completer port; TL-UL host port (32-bit data, OpenTitan profile); one outstanding request; full-strobe writes (PutFullData) and word reads (Get); back-to-back transfers with PSEL held high; error mapping to PSLVERR; one clock domain and one reset.

Excluded: partial writes (any PSTRB other than 4'b1111); byte or half-word accesses; TL-UL bursts and multiple outstanding requests; the TL-UL-to-APB direction; TL-UL bus integrity generation or checking; a response timeout (the SoC watchdog handles a device that never responds, DEC-003); address decoding or protection; clock-domain crossing; software-visible registers.
Item: Target SoC / product class; Specification: Microcontroller-class SoC with an OpenTitan-style TL-UL interconnect and an APB4 peripheral subsystem
Item: Technology / library assumptions; Specification: Synchronous digital standard-cell flow; no technology-specific cells (no memories, ICGs or synchronizers)
Item: Operating modes and workload; Specification: Low-rate control accesses with low latency; no streaming traffic
Item: Security / privilege context; Specification: No privilege decision in the bridge; protection is enforced by the TL-UL fabric (section 18)
Item: External dependencies; Specification: A protocol-compliant APB Requester; a TL-UL device or crossbar that returns exactly one response per request; a reset controller (DEP-001, DEP-002)

ID: REQ-FUNC-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the APB side is idle and i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 0 (Setup phase), the bridge shall capture the request at the rising edge that ends that cycle and, when the request is legal, shall present it on the TL-UL channel A from flip-flops in the next cycle (the first Access cycle).; Source: REF-001 4.1, Appendix A; DEC-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002, TEST-006; assertion SVA-008

ID: REQ-FUNC-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall convert an APB write with PSTRB = 4'b1111 and PADDR[1:0] = 2'b00 into one TL-UL PutFullData (a_opcode = 3'b000) with a_size = 2, a_mask = 4'b1111, a_address = PADDR and a_data = PWDATA.; Source: REF-002 usage of opcode, size and mask; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002; assertion SVA-004

ID: REQ-FUNC-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall convert an APB read with PADDR[1:0] = 2'b00 into one TL-UL Get (a_opcode = 3'b100) with a_size = 2, a_mask = 4'b1111 and a_address = PADDR. PSTRB is ignored on reads.; Source: REF-002; REF-001 3.2; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-006; assertion SVA-004

ID: REQ-FUNC-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall have at most one TL-UL request outstanding and shall start no new request before the APB completion of the previous transfer.; Source: DEC-002; REF-005 pendingReqPerSrc; Applies to: All; Verification method: Assertion SVA-003; simulation TEST-013

ID: REQ-FUNC-005; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall keep o_tlul_a_valid high and channel A stable from the cycle after capture until i_tlul_a_ready is sampled high.; Source: REF-002 timing diagrams; REF-005; Applies to: All; Verification method: Assertion SVA-002; simulation TEST-009

ID: REQ-FUNC-006; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall return the TL-UL d_data on o_apb_prdata for a read that completes without error and shall drive o_apb_prdata to 0 for a write completion and for every error completion.; Source: REF-001 3.3, 3.4; DEC-009; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002, TEST-006, TEST-007

ID: REQ-FUNC-007; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall discard a TL-UL response that arrives when no request has been accepted (orphan response) without any effect on the APB side.; Source: REF-002 explicit error cases (orphaned responses discarded on the host side); Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-010; assertion SVA-009

ID: REQ-FUNC-008; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall detect the Setup phase of a transfer from the levels i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 0 (not from an edge of i_apb_psel), and shall accept a new transfer whose Setup phase is in the cycle immediately after the PREADY cycle of the previous transfer, both when i_apb_psel stays 1 and only i_apb_penable changes level, and when i_apb_psel returns to 0 for one or more cycles in between. Every combination of read, write and error transfers shall be supported back to back.; Source: REF-001 3.1, 4.1 and Figure 4-1 (the bus moves directly from ACCESS to SETUP when another transfer follows); Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-019; assertion SVA-010

ID: REQ-IF-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall expose exactly the APB4 Completer signals listed in section 6.2 and no other APB signal.; Source: REF-001 chapter 2; REF-003 PRT-01, PRT-03; Applies to: All; Verification method: Lint and port-list review: TEST-016

ID: REQ-IF-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall expose exactly the TL-UL host signals listed in section 6.2 (the full OpenTitan signal set; d_param, d_size, d_sink and d_user are unused, DEC-006) and no other.; Source: REF-002 signals; DEC-006; Applies to: All; Verification method: Lint and port-list review: TEST-016

ID: REQ-IF-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: Every output port that changes value during operation shall be driven directly by the Q pin of a flip-flop, with no combinational logic between the flip-flop and the port. Outputs that never change after reset are constant tie-offs (DEC-005).; Source: Product requirement; DEC-005; Applies to: All; Verification method: Structural check of the RTL and the synthesized netlist: TEST-017

ID: REQ-IF-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall assert o_apb_pready for exactly one cycle per transfer, and only in an Access cycle (i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 1). o_apb_pslverr shall be 1 only while o_apb_pready is 1.; Source: REF-001 3.1, 3.4; Applies to: All; Verification method: Assertion SVA-001; APB protocol checker

ID: REQ-IF-005; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall drive o_tlul_a_param = 3'b000, o_tlul_a_size = 2'b10, o_tlul_a_mask = 4'b1111, o_tlul_a_source = PARA_SRC_ID and o_tlul_a_user = '0 (all bits zero) on every request.; Source: REF-002; DEC-004; Applies to: All; Verification method: Assertion SVA-005

ID: REQ-IF-006; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall drive o_tlul_d_ready low in reset and high from the first clock edge after reset release, and shall keep it high.; Source: DEC-010; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-001; assertion SVA-006

ID: REQ-IF-007; Requirement using shall/should/may: The APB-facing logic and the TL-UL-facing logic shall be in two separate modules that are connected only through the internal interface of section 5.1.; Source: Product requirement; Applies to: All; Verification method: Design review and hierarchy check: TEST-017

ID: REQ-ERR-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: When a write has PSTRB other than 4'b1111, the bridge shall issue no TL-UL request and shall complete the transfer with PREADY = 1 and PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle.; Source: DEC-001; REF-001 3.4; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-004

ID: REQ-ERR-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: When PADDR[1:0] is not 2'b00 (read or write), the bridge shall issue no TL-UL request and shall complete the transfer with PREADY = 1 and PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle.; Source: REF-001 chapter 2 (unaligned address UNPREDICTABLE); DEC-001; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-005

ID: REQ-ERR-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the TL-UL response has d_error = 1, the bridge shall complete the APB transfer with PSLVERR = 1.; Source: REF-002 explicit error cases; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-007

ID: REQ-ERR-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the TL-UL response has a d_opcode other than AccessAckData (3'b001) for a read, or other than AccessAck (3'b000) for a write, the bridge shall complete the APB transfer with PSLVERR = 1.; Source: REF-005 respOpcode; DEC-008; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-008

ID: REQ-ERR-005; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the TL-UL response has d_source different from PARA_SRC_ID, the bridge shall complete the APB transfer with PSLVERR = 1.; Source: REF-005 respMustHaveReq; DEC-008; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-008

ID: REQ-CLK-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall operate in one clock domain, i_clk_core, for both interfaces and shall contain no clock-domain crossing.; Source: Section 7; Applies to: All; Verification method: CDC analysis: TEST-016

ID: REQ-RESET-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall use the active-low reset i_rst_n_core with asynchronous assertion and shall drive o_tlul_a_valid, o_tlul_d_ready, o_apb_pready, o_apb_prdata, o_apb_pslverr, o_tlul_a_opcode, o_tlul_a_address and o_tlul_a_data to 0 while the reset is asserted.; Source: REF-003 RST-01; DEC-010, DEC-013; Applies to: All; Verification method: Reset test: TEST-001

ID: REQ-RESET-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall abandon any transfer in progress when the reset is asserted and shall send no APB completion for it after reset release.; Source: Section 7.3; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-012

ID: REQ-PARAM-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall accept only the parameter values listed in section 8; an illegal value shall be reported at elaboration of the verification source set.; Source: Section 8; Applies to: All; Verification method: Elaboration check: TEST-014

ID: REQ-PERF-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the TL-UL device accepts the request in the first cycle and returns the response in the following cycle, the APB Access phase shall last 3 cycles (2 wait states).; Source: Section 10.3; DEC-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002, TEST-006

ID: REQ-PERF-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the device returns the response in the cycle in which it accepts the request, the APB Access phase shall last 2 cycles (1 wait state).; Source: Section 10.3; REF-005 (response in the acceptance cycle allowed); Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-011

ID: REQ-PERF-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: A local error completion (REQ-ERR-001, REQ-ERR-002) shall last 1 Access cycle (no wait state), and a new Setup phase shall be accepted in the cycle after PREADY.; Source: Section 10.3, 10.4; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-004, TEST-005, TEST-013

ID: REQ-PERF-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: With i_apb_psel held high, back-to-back transfers shall run at the same minimum Setup-to-Setup interval as with a gap: 4 cycles with a prompt device, 3 cycles with a same-cycle response and 2 cycles after a local error, with no idle cycle added by the bridge.; Source: Section 10.4; REQ-FUNC-008; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-019

ID: REQ-RTL-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The RTL shall comply with REF-003 and shall use the hierarchy of section 14.2.; Source: REF-003; Applies to: All; Verification method: Lint and review: TEST-016

ID: REQ-VER-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: An APB protocol checker and the TL-UL protocol checker of REF-005 shall be bound to the ports in every simulation.; Source: REF-001, REF-005; Applies to: All; Verification method: Simulation log review: TEST-015

ID: REQ-DFT-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The RTL shall be scan-insertable: no latch, no combinational loop, no internal tri-state, no clock gating and no gated or derived clock.; Source: REF-003 section 11; Applies to: All; Verification method: Lint and scan rule check: TEST-018

The data width is fixed at 32 bits; there is no data-width parameter (DEC-011).
Values of PARA_ADDR_W outside 16 to 32 are illegal (section 8).
The bridge has two modules below a structural top.
The APB-facing module m_apb_if owns everything that depends on APB signals.
The TL-UL-facing module m_tlul_if owns everything that depends on TL-UL signals.
They exchange one request bundle and one response bundle through internal wires, so neither module reads a port of the other bus.

Early launch.
The APB manager already drives PADDR, PWRITE, PWDATA and PSTRB in the Setup phase, and keeps them unchanged until the transfer completes (REF-001 3.1, 4.1, Appendix A).
The bridge therefore captures the request at the end of the Setup cycle straight into the TL-UL channel A flip-flops.
Channel A is valid in the first Access cycle, so the request reaches the TL-UL device one cycle after the Setup cycle, with no intermediate buffer stage.
Setup (S): i_apb_psel = 1, i_apb_penable = 0.
The APB side is idle.
At the end of S, a legal request is loaded into the A-channel flops and reg_a_valid is set; an illegal request instead loads the response flops with PSLVERR = 1 and PREADY = 1.
Access 1 (A1): o_tlul_a_valid = 1 with the converted request, o_tlul_d_ready = 1.
When i_tlul_a_ready = 1 the request is accepted at the end of A1.
Access 2 (A2): the device returns the response (i_tlul_d_valid = 1).
At the end of A2 the response is checked and loaded into reg_prdata, reg_pslverr and reg_pready.
Access 3 (A3): o_apb_pready = 1 with o_apb_prdata and o_apb_pslverr, all from flops.
The transfer ends at the end of A3.
Next transfer: the next Setup phase may follow in the cycle after A3.
If the device answers in the cycle in which it accepts the request (A1), the response is loaded at the end of A1 and PREADY is 1 in A2.
If the device holds a_ready low, o_tlul_a_valid and channel A stay unchanged and the Access phase is extended; the same happens when the response is late.
Back-to-back transfers.

An APB Requester that has another transfer for the same Completer keeps i_apb_psel at 1 after the last Access cycle and only drives i_apb_penable back to 0; the bus then moves directly from ACCESS to SETUP (REF-001 3.1, 4.1).
The bridge supports this without any idle cycle.
The reason is that the Setup phase is recognized by the levels i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 0 while the APB FSM is idle, not by a rising edge of i_apb_psel.
The PREADY cycle of a transfer is also the cycle in which the APB FSM is in ENUM_ST_DONE, and the APB FSM is in ENUM_ST_IDLE again in the next cycle, which is the Setup cycle of the next transfer.
The A-channel flops, the response flops and both FSMs are therefore free in time for the next capture, and the next transfer starts exactly like the first one.
The same holds when the Requester releases i_apb_psel for one or more cycles in between.
Figure 6-4 shows a write, a read and an illegal write one after the other with i_apb_psel held high.
At most one TL-UL request is outstanding, and its a_source is PARA_SRC_ID.
o_tlul_a_valid is high only in the TL-UL FSM state ENUM_ST_REQ, and channel A does not change while o_tlul_a_valid is high and i_tlul_a_ready is low.
o_apb_pready is high only in the APB FSM state ENUM_ST_DONE, for one cycle.
No TL-UL request is issued for an illegal APB request.
The TL-UL FSM is idle whenever the APB FSM is idle.

Port names follow REF-003 PRT-01: i_ or o_, then the protocol tag, then the signal mnemonic, with the tag apb for APB and the tag tlul for TL-UL (REF-003 has no TL-UL entry).
The clock and reset are named i_clk_core and i_rst_n_core because one clock serves both buses (DEC-012).
The TL-UL signal set is the OpenTitan tl_h2d_t and tl_d2h_t set, flattened.
The inputs d_param, d_size, d_sink and d_user are present for integration but no logic reads them (DEC-006).
Output ports marked "flop" come directly from a flip-flop; ports marked "constant" are tie-offs (DEC-005).

The Completer is single-transfer.
The Setup phase lasts one cycle (PSEL = 1, PENABLE = 0); the Access phase starts in the next cycle and lasts until PREADY is high (REF-001 4.1).
The signals PADDR, PWRITE, PWDATA and PSTRB stay unchanged from Setup until PREADY (REF-001 3.1, 4.1), which lets the bridge capture them once, at the Setup edge.
PSLVERR is only valid in the last cycle of the transfer (REF-001 3.4), and the bridge asserts it only together with PREADY.
PSTRB is LOW on reads (REF-001 3.2) and is ignored by the bridge on reads.
Back-to-back transfers with i_apb_psel held high are supported (REQ-FUNC-008, section 5.3).

A response in the same cycle as the request acceptance is allowed by REF-005 and is supported.

Cycle / event: Next cycle; Input condition: i_apb_psel = 0, or the next Setup phase; State/action: APB FSM to ENUM_ST_IDLE; Output condition: reg_pready and reg_pslverr cleared
Variants: a response in A1 (the cycle of acceptance) gives o_apb_pready = 1 in A2, a 2-cycle Access phase (REQ-PERF-002).
A local error loads reg_pready at the end of S, so o_apb_pready = 1 in A1, a 1-cycle Access phase (REQ-PERF-003, Figure 12-2).
A device that holds a_ready low or answers late extends the Access phase by the same number of cycles.

For back-to-back transfers the Setup cycle of the next transfer is the cycle after the PREADY cycle, with i_apb_psel still 1 and i_apb_penable = 0; the APB FSM is in ENUM_ST_IDLE in that cycle and captures the request at its end (Figure 6-4).
*Figure 10-1.
The device answers in the cycle in which it accepts the request: 2 Access cycles (source: figures/apb_write_same_cycle.json).*
*Figure 10-2.
Reset and release: all flop outputs are 0 in reset; o_tlul_d_ready becomes 1 at the first clock edge after release (source: figures/reset_sequence.json).*
*Figure 10-3. d_valid at T1 (idle), T3 (before acceptance) and T7 (after the response) is discarded; the real response is at T5 (source: figures/tlul_orphan_response.json).*
There is no arbitration and no buffer: one request is outstanding.
The earliest next Setup phase is the cycle after PREADY, because the APB FSM is back in ENUM_ST_IDLE by then.
The minimum interval between the starts of two transfers is therefore 4 cycles with a prompt device (S plus 3 Access cycles), 3 cycles with a same-cycle response, and 2 cycles for a local error.
The same intervals apply when i_apb_psel stays high between transfers (REQ-FUNC-008, REQ-PERF-004): the bridge adds no idle cycle, because it needs only the PREADY cycle to return to idle.

ID: ASM-002; Type: Assumption; Assumption / dependency / unresolved decision: The TL-UL device returns exactly one response per request and no response before acceptance, and obeys REF-005; Technical impact / version / configuration: A device that never answers blocks the bridge (DEC-003); Resolution / status: Open; integration check

ID: ASM-003; Type: Assumption; Assumption / dependency / unresolved decision: Data width 32 bits (DW = 32, DBW = 4, SZW = 2) and the OpenTitan default of 8-bit source ID; Technical impact / version / configuration: Section 6.2; Resolution / status: Announced to the designer, not contested

ID: ASM-004; Type: Assumption; Assumption / dependency / unresolved decision: The module is named m_apb_tlul_bridge; TL-UL ports use the tag tlul; Technical impact / version / configuration: Section 6.2; Resolution / status: Announced to the designer, not contested

ID: ASM-005; Type: Assumption; Assumption / dependency / unresolved decision: A width parameter PARA_A_USER_W is needed to declare o_tlul_a_user; it was not in the parameter list the designer approved (answer 4A). The parameter PARA_A_USER was removed on 2026-10-18 and o_tlul_a_user is driven to '0; Technical impact / version / configuration: One extra parameter, no behavior; Resolution / status: Confirmed by the designer, 2026-10-18; default width 1 (lowest) because the bits carry a fixed value

ID: DEC-001; Type: Decision; Assumption / dependency / unresolved decision: Only full-strobe writes (PSTRB = 4'b1111) and word-aligned addresses are accepted; every other write PSTRB (including 4'b0000) and every misaligned address returns PSLVERR with no TL-UL request; Technical impact / version / configuration: Partial writes are not available through this bridge. TL-UL PutPartialData is never issued; Resolution / status: Confirmed by the designer, 2026-10-18

ID: DEC-002; Type: Decision; Assumption / dependency / unresolved decision: Single outstanding request; early launch: the request is captured at the Setup edge so that channel A is valid in the first Access cycle; Technical impact / version / configuration: 3 Access cycles with a prompt device; a_valid comes from a flop; Resolution / status: Confirmed by the designer, 2026-10-18

ID: DEC-003; Type: Decision; Assumption / dependency / unresolved decision: No timeout and no drain mechanism; the SoC watchdog handles a device that never answers; Technical impact / version / configuration: The APB Requester waits indefinitely (ERR-006); Resolution / status: Confirmed by the designer, 2026-10-18

ID: DEC-004; Type: Decision; Assumption / dependency / unresolved decision: a_user is driven to zero (no parameter); no TL-UL bus integrity is generated or checked; Technical impact / version / configuration: See OI-001; Resolution / status: Confirmed by the designer, 2026-10-18

ID: DEC-005; Type: Decision; Assumption / dependency / unresolved decision: "Every output comes from a flip-flop" is applied to all outputs that can change. Outputs that never change after reset (a_param, a_size, a_mask, a_source, a_user, a_opcode[1:0], a_address[1:0]) are constant tie-offs, not flip-flops; Technical impact / version / configuration: They have no logic and no glitch; adding flops with a constant D input would be removed by synthesis; Resolution / status: Confirmed by the designer, 2026-10-18 (tie-off, no flip-flop needed)

ID: DEC-006; Type: Decision; Assumption / dependency / unresolved decision: The ports d_param, d_size, d_sink and d_user are present but unused; d_size and d_param are not checked. The width-only parameters PARA_D_SINK_W and PARA_D_USER_W default to 1 (lowest); Technical impact / version / configuration: The full OpenTitan port set eases integration; unused inputs need a lint waiver; Resolution / status: Port presence confirmed by the designer, 2026-10-18; the two width parameters were added by the author, confirm

ID: DEC-007; Type: Decision; Assumption / dependency / unresolved decision: PPROT is accepted and ignored; Technical impact / version / configuration: No privilege or instruction-fetch information reaches TL-UL (a_user is zero); Resolution / status: Announced, not contested

When the APB side is idle and i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 0 (Setup phase), the bridge shall capture the request at the rising edge that ends that cycle and, when the request is legal, shall present it on the TL-UL channel A from flip-flops in the next cycle (the first Access cycle).

The bridge shall convert an APB write with PSTRB = 4'b1111 and PADDR[1:0] = 2'b00 into one TL-UL PutFullData (a_opcode = 3'b000) with a_size = 2, a_mask = 4'b1111, a_address = PADDR and a_data = PWDATA.
REF-002 usage of opcode, size and mask
The bridge shall convert an APB read with PADDR[1:0] = 2'b00 into one TL-UL Get (a_opcode = 3'b100) with a_size = 2, a_mask = 4'b1111 and a_address = PADDR. PSTRB is ignored on reads.
The bridge shall have at most one TL-UL request outstanding and shall start no new request before the APB completion of the previous transfer.
The bridge shall keep o_tlul_a_valid high and channel A stable from the cycle after capture until i_tlul_a_ready is sampled high.
The bridge shall return the TL-UL d_data on o_apb_prdata for a read that completes without error and shall drive o_apb_prdata to 0 for a write completion and for every error completion.
The bridge shall discard a TL-UL response that arrives when no request has been accepted (orphan response) without any effect on the APB side.
REF-002 explicit error cases (orphaned responses discarded on the host side)

The bridge shall detect the Setup phase of a transfer from the levels i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 0 (not from an edge of i_apb_psel), and shall accept a new transfer whose Setup phase is in the cycle immediately after the PREADY cycle of the previous transfer, both when i_apb_psel stays 1 and only i_apb_penable changes level, and when i_apb_psel returns to 0 for one or more cycles in between. Every combination of read, write and error transfers shall be supported back to back.
REF-001 3.1, 4.1 and Figure 4-1 (the bus moves directly from ACCESS to SETUP when another transfer follows)
The bridge shall expose exactly the APB4 Completer signals listed in section 6.2 and no other APB signal.
The bridge shall expose exactly the TL-UL host signals listed in section 6.2 (the full OpenTitan signal set; d_param, d_size, d_sink and d_user are unused, DEC-006) and no other.

Every output port that changes value during operation shall be driven directly by the Q pin of a flip-flop, with no combinational logic between the flip-flop and the port. Outputs that never change after reset are constant tie-offs (DEC-005).
Structural check of the RTL and the synthesized netlist: TEST-017
The bridge shall assert o_apb_pready for exactly one cycle per transfer, and only in an Access cycle (i_apb_psel = 1 and i_apb_penable = 1). o_apb_pslverr shall be 1 only while o_apb_pready is 1.
The bridge shall drive o_tlul_a_param = 3'b000, o_tlul_a_size = 2'b10, o_tlul_a_mask = 4'b1111, o_tlul_a_source = PARA_SRC_ID and o_tlul_a_user = '0 (all bits zero) on every request.
The bridge shall drive o_tlul_d_ready low in reset and high from the first clock edge after reset release, and shall keep it high.
The APB-facing logic and the TL-UL-facing logic shall be in two separate modules that are connected only through the internal interface of section 5.1.
Design review and hierarchy check: TEST-017
When a write has PSTRB other than 4'b1111, the bridge shall issue no TL-UL request and shall complete the transfer with PREADY = 1 and PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle.
When PADDR[1:0] is not 2'b00 (read or write), the bridge shall issue no TL-UL request and shall complete the transfer with PREADY = 1 and PSLVERR = 1 in the first Access cycle.
When the TL-UL response has d_error = 1, the bridge shall complete the APB transfer with PSLVERR = 1.
When the TL-UL response has a d_opcode other than AccessAckData (3'b001) for a read, or other than AccessAck (3'b000) for a write, the bridge shall complete the APB transfer with PSLVERR = 1.
When the TL-UL response has d_source different from PARA_SRC_ID, the bridge shall complete the APB transfer with PSLVERR = 1.
The bridge shall operate in one clock domain, i_clk_core, for both interfaces and shall contain no clock-domain crossing.

The bridge shall use the active-low reset i_rst_n_core with asynchronous assertion and shall drive o_tlul_a_valid, o_tlul_d_ready, o_apb_pready, o_apb_prdata, o_apb_pslverr, o_tlul_a_opcode, o_tlul_a_address and o_tlul_a_data to 0 while the reset is asserted.
The bridge shall abandon any transfer in progress when the reset is asserted and shall send no APB completion for it after reset release.
The bridge shall accept only the parameter values listed in section 8; an illegal value shall be reported at elaboration of the verification source set.
When the TL-UL device accepts the request in the first cycle and returns the response in the following cycle, the APB Access phase shall last 3 cycles (2 wait states).
When the device returns the response in the cycle in which it accepts the request, the APB Access phase shall last 2 cycles (1 wait state).
Section 10.3; REF-005 (response in the acceptance cycle allowed)
A local error completion (REQ-ERR-001, REQ-ERR-002) shall last 1 Access cycle (no wait state), and a new Setup phase shall be accepted in the cycle after PREADY.

With i_apb_psel held high, back-to-back transfers shall run at the same minimum Setup-to-Setup interval as with a gap: 4 cycles with a prompt device, 3 cycles with a same-cycle response and 2 cycles after a local error, with no idle cycle added by the bridge.
The RTL shall comply with REF-003 and shall use the hierarchy of section 14.2.
An APB protocol checker and the TL-UL protocol checker of REF-005 shall be bound to the ports in every simulation.
The RTL shall be scan-insertable: no latch, no combinational loop, no internal tri-state, no clock gating and no gated or derived clock.
